cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the church of God in Corinth (2 Corinthians 1:1). He's just told them that our outer self is wasting away, but our inner self is being renewed day by day (2 Corinthians 4:16). Now he gives a picture for the body we live in: an earthly tent.

cards.question: Paul says that if this earthly tent we live in is dismantled, we have something from God. What is it?

answers.text: A longer stay in this tent

cards.question: Paul says this eternal house in heaven was built by human hands.

cards.text: A tent comes down, but this house is eternal. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer watching my edges go soft, so trust me, I KNOW tent life.
Paul says in this tent we groan. Me? I groan just leaning down to peek in the oven, and NOBODY approved that noise.

cards.question: While we groan in this earthly tent, what does Paul say we're longing for?

answers.text: To be clothed with our heavenly dwelling
To make this tent last a lot longer
To be left alone to rest in the tent

cards.question: Paul is talking about being clothed with our heavenly dwelling. When we're clothed, what does he say we won't be found?

cards.text: Paul comes back to it: while we're in this tent, we groan under our burdens. But he's crystal clear about what he's after.

cards.question: Paul says that while we groan under our burdens in this tent, we wish to be unclothed.
We don't wish to be unclothed but clothed, so that our mortality may be swallowed up by ___.

cards.text: So who got us ready for all of this? Paul says it's God who prepared us for this very purpose.

cards.question: God prepared us for this very purpose. What does Paul say God has given us as a pledge of what is to come?

cards.text: And a pledge from God is NOT a group chat "on my way" typed from under the covers. We ALL know that "on my way," friend, and this ain't it.
Now here's the catch, friend. Paul says that while we're at home in the body, we're away from the Lord.

cards.question: Even though we're away from the Lord while we're at home in the body, Paul says we are always confident.
Paul is confident even while he's away from the Lord. How does he say we walk?

answers.text: By faith and not by sight
By sight and not by faith

cards.text: Walking by faith is like heading to the kitchen at 2 a.m. with the lights off. You can't SEE the counter, but baby, you KNOW it's there.

cards.question: Paul says we are confident, and would prefer to be away from the ___ and at home with the ___.
Whether we're at home in this body or away from it, what does Paul say we aspire to do?

cards.text: Then Paul gives the reason. And friend, this one makes me stand up straight on my gold base and fix my hat.

cards.question: Paul says we must all appear somewhere. Where is it?

answers.text: Before the judgment seat of Christ

cards.question: At the judgment seat of Christ, Paul says each one receives his due only for the good things done in the body.

findings.problem: This card recaps what cards 2 and 3 already covered ('A tent comes down, but this house is eternal') and then makes a joke. It tells nothing new from the passage and doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The card says Papa Dorin spent years in the junk drawer 'watching my edges go soft.' His backstory says his edges went soft from years of baking on the Millers' counter, before he went into the drawer. The line changes his backstory.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The right answer uses the passage's own wording ('clothed with our heavenly dwelling'). Both wrong answers sound casual and modern ('a lot longer', 'left alone to rest'). The right answer stands out as the Bible-sounding one.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: This card is only a joke about the pledge from card 12. It tells no part of the passage and doesn't move the baker forward. The joke should ride along on a card that tells the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This card is only a joke comparison for 'walk by faith, not by sight,' which card 3 already covered. It tells no new part of the passage and doesn't move the baker forward.
